topics.t: Solid shapes in monuments and models
topics.h: India Gate, Qutub Minar and even your school building are made of solid shapes hiding in plain sight!
p: Big buildings are made of solid shapes: cuboids, cubes, cylinders, cones, spheres, prisms and pyramids.
Qutub Minar looks like tall cylinders stacked one on another, getting thinner at the top.
To build a model, pick the block whose shape matches each part: a cuboid for a wall, a cylinder for a pillar, a cone or pyramid for a pointed top.
A model looks like the real thing in shape, but it is much smaller and made of different material.
You can make a street model from waste: boxes for houses, bottles and tubes for towers, bottle caps for wheels.

ex.q: Neha builds a model gate with blocks. She needs 2 tall pillars and a flat top piece across them. Which blocks should she choose?
st: Pillars are tall and round or tall and straight: cylinders or long cuboids work.
The top piece is a long flat block lying across: a cuboid.
So 2 cylinders (or tall cuboids) and 1 long cuboid.
ex.a: 2 cylinders for the pillars and 1 long cuboid on top

topics.rl: Next time you pass a temple, a water tank or a bus stop, name the solid shapes in it: the dome, the tank, the pillars and the roof.

rv.summary: Big buildings are made of solid shapes like cuboids, cylinders, cones and pyramids. To build a model, pick the block whose shape matches each part; a model has the same shape but is much smaller.
focus: Name the solid shapes in monuments: Qutub Minar looks like stacked cylinders, a dome is like half a sphere
Choose the right block for each part of a model
Know how a model is different from the real thing
Count all the blocks used, including the top piece
remember: Cuboid for a wall, cylinder for a pillar, cone or pyramid for a pointed top
A model looks like the real thing in shape, but it is much smaller and made of different material
traps: Don't think every tall building is a pyramid
A model does not change the shape of the building, only its size and material
Don't forget to count the cone on top

topics.h: Open up a sweet box and lay it flat. What shape do you get? That flat shape is called a net!
p: A net is a flat shape that can be folded to make a 3D shape.
The net of a cube has 6 squares. The net of a cuboid has 6 rectangles.
The net of a cylinder has 2 circles and 1 rectangle.
The net of a square pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles.
The top view is what you see from straight above. The front view is what you see from the front.

ex.q: A glass shaped like a cylinder stands on a table. What do you see from the top and from the front?
st: From straight above, you see the round rim: a circle.
From the front, you see a straight side, top and bottom: a rectangle.
ex.a: Top view: circle. Front view: rectangle.

topics.rl: Sweet boxes, gift boxes and toothpaste boxes are made by folding flat cardboard nets.

rv.summary: A net is a flat shape that folds to make a 3D shape. The top view is what you see from straight above and the front view is what you see from the front.
focus: Match nets to shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, square pyramid
Count the squares or rectangles in a net
Tell the top view from the front view of a solid
remember: Net of a cube: 6 squares. Net of a cuboid: 6 rectangles
Net of a cylinder: 2 circles and 1 rectangle
Net of a square pyramid: 1 square and 4 triangles
Cylinder glass: top view circle, front view rectangle
traps: Don't forget the top and bottom faces when counting a net
Don't give the top view (circle) when the front view of a cone (triangle) is asked
Don't give a different view for a sphere: it looks like a circle from every direction

topics.h: A camping tent and a tent-shaped chocolate bar are both prisms. The great tombs of Egypt are pyramids. What makes them different?
p: A prism has two matching end faces (bases) joined by rectangle side faces.
A pyramid has one base. Its side faces are triangles that meet at one point called the apex.
We name them by the shape of the base: triangular prism, square pyramid, pentagonal prism and so on.
A cube is a special prism: all 6 of its faces are equal squares.
You can make prisms and pyramids by folding their nets and sticking the edges.

ex.q: A solid has 2 pentagon faces and 5 rectangle faces. What is it called?
st: Two matching end faces joined by rectangles means it is a prism.
So it is a pentagonal prism.

topics.rl: A camping tent is a triangular prism. A pencil box is a rectangular prism (cuboid). The roof of some temples is a pyramid.

rv.summary: A prism has two matching end faces joined by rectangle side faces. A pyramid has one base and triangle side faces that meet at a point called the apex.
focus: Tell prisms and pyramids apart by their side faces
Name them by the shape of the base
Count faces: the base shape's sides give the number of rectangles or triangles
remember: Prism: 2 matching bases + rectangle side faces
Pyramid: 1 base + triangle side faces meeting at the apex
A cube is a special prism with 6 equal square faces
Triangular prism: 2 + 3 = 5 faces
traps: Don't count the base as a triangle side face
Don't give a prism triangle side faces: pyramids have triangle sides, prisms have rectangle sides
Don't confuse the apex with the base

topics.t: Solid 3D shapes: faces, edges and corners
topics.h: A laddoo rolls, but a dice does not. Why? Let us find out!
p: A 3D shape is solid. It has length, width and height. You can hold it.
A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A corner is where edges meet.
A cube (like a dice) has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A cuboid (like a brick) also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere (like a laddoo) is round all over. A cylinder (like a tin) has 2 flat faces and a curved surface. A cone (like a party cap) has 1 flat face and a pointed tip.

ex.q: A matchbox is a cuboid. How many faces, edges and corners does it have?
st: Count the flat faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, right = 6
Count the edges: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom, 4 standing = 12
Count the corners: 4 on top and 4 on the bottom = 8

topics.rl: Your geometry box is a cuboid, a ball is a sphere, a pipe is a cylinder and an ice-cream cone is a cone.

rv.summary: A 3D shape is solid and has faces, edges and corners. A cube and a cuboid both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
focus: Know what a face, an edge and a corner are
Count faces, edges and corners of a cube and a cuboid
Name everyday solids: sphere, cylinder, cone, cube, cuboid
remember: Face: a flat surface. Edge: where two faces meet. Corner: where edges meet
Cube and cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners
Cylinder: 2 flat faces and a curved surface. Cone: 1 flat face and a pointed tip
traps: Don't count corners (8) when edges (12) are asked
Don't count the curved side of a cylinder as a flat face
Don't mix up the cone and the cylinder

topics.t: Building solids with straws and clay
topics.h: With straws and small clay balls you can build the skeleton of a cube, and discover a secret number pattern!
p: In a straw model, each straw is an edge and each clay ball is a corner.
A cube skeleton needs 12 straws and 8 clay balls. A square pyramid needs 8 straws and 5 balls.
For solids with only flat faces: faces + corners − edges = 2. For a cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
A solid with only flat faces needs at least 4 faces. So no such solid has exactly 3 flat faces.
Paper strips joined crossing at the top and bottom, then spread out, make a ball-like sphere.

ex.q: Sana has 6 straws and 4 clay balls. Which solid skeleton can she make using all of them?
st: A triangular pyramid has 6 edges and 4 corners.
So she can make a triangular pyramid.

topics.rl: Builders first make a frame of iron rods and joints, just like a straw skeleton, before adding walls.

rv.summary: In a straw model, each straw is an edge and each clay ball is a corner. For solids with only flat faces, faces + corners − edges = 2.
focus: Find how many straws and clay balls a skeleton needs
Use faces + corners − edges = 2 to find a missing number
Know that a solid with only flat faces needs at least 4 faces
remember: Straw = edge, clay ball = corner
Cube: 12 straws, 8 balls. Square pyramid: 8 straws, 5 balls
faces + corners − edges = 2 (cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2)
traps: Don't mix up edges with corners
Don't forget the straws that go up to the apex
Don't add 2 instead of taking it away in the pattern

topics.h: Next time you play Ludo, look closely at the dice. Its numbers hide a magic total!
p: On a standard dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7.
So 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, and 3 is opposite 4.
Each face touches 4 other faces along its edges. These are its neighbours (adjacent faces).
Only the opposite face does not share an edge with a face.
Faces you see together in one view are neighbours, so they cannot be opposite each other.

ex.q: A dice shows 2 on top. What number is at the bottom?
st: Top and bottom are opposite faces.

topics.rl: In board games like Ludo and Snakes and Ladders, the dice is made fair by putting each number opposite its partner that makes 7.

rv.summary: On a standard dice, opposite faces always add up to 7. Every face touches 4 neighbours; only the opposite face does not share an edge with it.
focus: Find the bottom face from the top face
Find hidden faces and their total
Use views: faces seen together are neighbours, not opposites
remember: Opposite faces add up to 7: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4
traps: Don't think the next number is opposite
Faces seen together cannot be opposite each other
Don't add the top faces when the bottom faces are asked

topics.h: A cube, a cone and a ball walk into a sorting game. Which group does each one join?
p: We can sort solids by their faces: only flat faces, only a curved surface, or both flat and curved.
Two overlapping circles (a Venn diagram) help sort by two rules at once, like 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'.
A shape that fits both rules goes in the overlap in the middle. A shape that fits neither goes outside both circles.
The shapes of the faces tell solids apart: a cube has only squares; a square pyramid has a square and triangles.
Clues about faces, edges and corners can name a solid: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 corners is a square pyramid.

ex.q: Where does a square pyramid go if one circle is 'has square faces' and the other is 'has triangle faces'?
st: It has a square base, so it fits the first circle.
It has triangle sides, so it fits the second circle.
It fits both, so it goes in the overlap.

topics.rl: Shopkeepers stack tins (cylinders) and boxes (cuboids) differently. Balls go in a basket because they roll!

rv.summary: Solids can be sorted by their faces: only flat, only curved, or both. A Venn diagram sorts by two rules at once, with the overlap for shapes that fit both.
focus: Sort solids: only flat faces, only curved surface, or both
Place shapes in a Venn diagram, including the overlap and outside
Name a solid from clues about faces, edges and corners
remember: Sphere: only a curved surface. Cylinder: flat faces and a curved surface
Fits both rules: overlap. Fits neither: outside both circles
5 faces, 8 edges, 5 corners is a square pyramid
traps: Don't forget that cylinders and cones have flat faces
Don't put a shape in the overlap until you have checked it fits both rules
Not every shape must go inside a circle

topics.t: Cube towers, dot paper and net puzzles
topics.h: Some cubes in a tower are hiding! Can you count the ones you cannot see?
p: When cubes are stacked, some cubes are hidden behind or below others. Count layer by layer.
A block 2 cubes long, 2 wide and 2 high has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cubes, even though one is hidden from view.
On triangular (isometric) dot paper, a cube is drawn with 3 faces showing: the top and two sides.
A cube net must have exactly 6 squares. 6 squares in one straight line will NOT fold into a cube.
If a net has only 5 squares, one face is missing and the box stays open.

ex.q: Arjun builds a 2 by 2 square layer of cubes and puts 1 cube on top in the middle of one corner. How many cubes in all?

topics.rl: Gift boxes and sweet boxes come flat from the factory as nets. The shopkeeper folds them up when you buy sweets.

rv.summary: When cubes are stacked, some are hidden, so count layer by layer. A cube net must have exactly 6 squares, and 6 squares in one straight line will not fold into a cube.
focus: Count cubes in towers and blocks, including hidden ones
Know how a cube looks on triangular dot paper
Decide which nets fold into a cube
remember: 2 × 2 × 2 block = 8 cubes
On triangular dot paper a cube shows 3 faces: the top and two sides
A cube net needs exactly 6 squares; 5 squares leaves the box open
traps: Don't count only the cubes you can see
Not every set of 6 squares makes a cube: a straight line of 6 will not fold
Don't leave out the hidden tower

topics.h: Open a book a little, then a lot. The opening between the covers is an angle!
p: An angle is made where two lines or edges meet at a point.
Angles are all around us: the corner of a book, the hands of a clock, an open door, scissors.
Fold a paper once, then fold it again so the folded edge lies on itself. The corner you get is a right angle checker.
A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book, a door or a table.
On a dot grid, two lines going straight across and straight up from the same dot make a right angle.

ex.q: How many angles are there in a square drawn on a dot grid?
st: At each corner two sides meet and make an angle.
So it has 4 angles, all right angles.

topics.rl: Carpenters check that the corners of a door frame are right angles, or the door will not shut properly!

rv.summary: An angle is made where two lines or edges meet at a point. A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book, and you can check it with a folded-paper checker.
focus: Know what an angle is and spot angles around us
Make and use a right angle checker
Count angles in shapes
remember: An angle is made where two lines meet at a point
Right angle = square corner
Right angle checker: fold paper once, then fold the folded edge onto itself
traps: One fold is not enough to make a right angle checker
A straight line is not a right angle
Not only a square has right angles: a rectangle has 4 too

topics.h: Is the tip of your pizza slice sharp or wide? Angles come in three sizes!
p: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle, like the tip of a pizza slice.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line, like a wide-open hand fan.
Use your right angle checker: if the angle fits inside it, it is acute; if the angle is wider, it is obtuse.
Capital letters have angles too. V and A have acute angles. L has a right angle.
Clues about angles can name a shape: 4 sides, all right angles, and equal sides means a square.

ex.q: Clock hands at 2:00. Is the angle acute, right or obtuse?
st: At 3:00 the hands make a right angle.
At 2:00 the hands are closer together.
So the angle is smaller than a right angle: acute.

topics.rl: A slide in the park, the open lid of a laptop, and a ladder against a wall all make angles of different sizes.

rv.summary: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle and an obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line. Use a right angle checker to compare.
focus: Sort angles into acute, right and obtuse
Find angle types on clocks and in capital letters
Name shapes from clues about their angles
remember: Acute: smaller than a right angle
Obtuse: bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line
V and A have acute angles; L has a right angle
traps: Don't mix up the names acute and obtuse
Equal sides do not always mean a square: a rhombus has 4 equal sides with acute and obtuse angles

topics.h: A rangoli tile, a kite and a roti are all flat shapes. Can you count their sides and corners?
p: A 2D shape is flat. You can draw it on paper.
A side is a straight line on the edge of a shape. A corner is where two sides meet.
Triangle: 3 sides. Square and rectangle: 4 sides. Pentagon: 5 sides. Hexagon: 6 sides.
A circle has one curved edge and no corners.
In a closed shape made of straight sides, the number of sides and corners is the same.

ex.q: Kabir draws a hexagon and a triangle. How many sides do they have altogether?

topics.rl: Look at floor tiles, a carrom board, road signs and a kite. Each one is a flat shape you can name by counting its sides.

rv.summary: A 2D shape is flat and can be drawn on paper. We name it by counting its straight sides; in a closed shape of straight sides, sides and corners are the same in number.
focus: Name shapes by their number of sides
Count total sides or corners of several shapes
Tell flat 2D shapes from solid 3D objects
remember: Triangle 3 sides, square and rectangle 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6
A circle has one curved edge and no corners
Sides and corners are the same in number in a closed shape of straight sides
traps: Don't mix up pentagon (5) and hexagon (6)
Don't count corners on a circle: it has 0 corners
An object with a square face is not a 2D shape

topics.h: Push a straw square and it squashes. Push a straw triangle and it stays strong. Why?
p: A triangle made of straws keeps its shape when pushed. It is rigid (strong).
A square or rectangle of straws can be pushed out of shape. Its sides stay the same, but its angles change.
Rectangles and squares are 4-sided shapes with all four angles right angles.
A 5-sided straw shape (pentagon) also changes its angles when pushed.
We can group shapes by how many angles they have: fewer than 5 (triangles, 4-sided shapes) or more than 5 (hexagons, octagons).

ex.q: Mohan pushes a straw square at one corner. What changes and what stays the same?
st: The straws do not stretch, so the side lengths stay the same.
The corners lean over, so the angles change.
The square becomes a slanted shape with 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles.
ex.a: Sides stay the same, angles change

topics.rl: Bridges, electric towers and bicycle frames use triangles because triangles do not bend out of shape.

rv.summary: A straw triangle is rigid and keeps its shape when pushed. A straw square, rectangle or pentagon can be pushed out of shape: its sides stay the same but its angles change.
focus: Know why triangles are used in bridges and towers
Tell what changes when a 4- or 5-sided straw shape is pushed
Group shapes by their number of angles
remember: A triangle is rigid (strong)
Rectangles and squares have all four angles right angles
A shape has as many angles as sides
traps: Squares are not the strongest shape; triangles are
Pushing a straw shape changes the angles, not the side lengths
Not every 4-sided shape with right angles is a square

topics.t: Amazing circles: centre, radius and diameter
topics.h: Put many equal straws around one point and their ends trace a perfect circle. Magic? No, maths!
p: Every point on a circle is the same distance from its centre, the middle point.
You can draw a circle by marking many points at the same distance from a centre and joining them smoothly.
The radius is a line from the centre to the edge. The diameter is a line across the circle through the centre.
Fold a circle in half to find a diameter. All diameters meet at the centre and are equal.
Diameter = 2 × radius. Radius = half of the diameter.

ex.q: A bicycle wheel has spokes 30 cm long from the centre to the rim. How wide is the wheel across the middle?
st: A spoke from centre to rim is a radius: 30 cm.
Across the middle is the diameter.

topics.rl: Bangles, wheels, rotis and round rangoli designs are all circles. A round carpet design has a centre with lines going out like radii.

rv.summary: Every point on a circle is the same distance from its centre. The radius goes from the centre to the edge, and the diameter goes across through the centre and is 2 × radius.
focus: Find the diameter from the radius and the radius from the diameter
Know that all diameters meet at the centre and are equal
Compare circles when one gives a radius and one a diameter
remember: Diameter = 2 × radius. Radius = half of the diameter
Fold a circle in half to find a diameter
traps: Don't halve the radius to get the diameter
Don't compare a radius with a diameter directly
A circle has very many diameters, not just one

topics.t: Shape puzzles: hidden shapes, cuts and paths
topics.h: A square with both its diagonals drawn hides 8 triangles. Can you find them all?
p: Big pictures hide smaller shapes. Look for shapes made of one piece, then of two or more pieces together.
One diagonal cuts a square into 2 triangles. Both diagonals cut it into 4 triangles.
A triangle can be cut on a dot grid into a square and smaller triangles.
To count all triangles, count small ones first, then the bigger ones made by joining pieces.
To trace a figure without lifting your pencil or repeating a line, start at a point where an odd number of lines meet.

ex.q: A triangle has one line drawn from its top corner down to its base. How many triangles are there in all?
st: The whole big triangle is also a triangle.

topics.rl: Matchstick puzzles, tangram sets and kolam patterns are all fun shape puzzles. Kolam artists draw some patterns in one go without lifting their hand!

rv.summary: Big pictures hide smaller shapes, so count small shapes first and then bigger ones made by joining pieces. To trace a figure in one go, start where an odd number of lines meet.
focus: Count all triangles in a figure, small and big
Know what diagonal cuts of a square make
Solve matchstick and one-stroke tracing puzzles
remember: One diagonal cuts a square into 2 triangles; both diagonals cut it into 4 small triangles
Start tracing at a point where an odd number of lines meet
traps: Don't count only the small triangles
Triangles side by side share sticks, so each new triangle does not need 3 new sticks
Don't start tracing at a point with an even number of lines

topics.t: Hide and seek: who can see what?
topics.h: In hide and seek, the best hiding spot is one the seeker cannot see. Where would you hide?
p: Position words tell where things are: behind, in front of, beside, above, below, between, under.
From where you stand, things hidden behind a wall, a tree or a big object cannot be seen.
If you move to a new spot, you may see things that were hidden before.
From high above, like from a rooftop or a tree, you can see things that are hidden from the ground.

ex.q: Raju hides behind a big water tank. Meera stands in front of the tank. Can Meera see Raju?
st: The tank is between Meera and Raju.

topics.rl: When you play hide and seek at a wedding or in a park, you choose spots behind pillars, cars or bushes so the seeker cannot see you.

rv.summary: Position words like behind, in front of, beside, above, below, between and under tell where things are. Things behind a big object are hidden, but moving to a new spot or looking from high above can show them.
focus: Use position words correctly
Decide who can see whom when something is in between
Know that moving or going higher changes what you can see
remember: Position words: behind, in front of, beside, above, below, between, under
From high above you can see things hidden from the ground
traps: Don't mix up above and below
Don't forget that things in between block the view
A hidden thing does not stay hidden from every spot

topics.h: A bird on a tree and an ant on the ground look at the same bucket. Do they see the same shape?
p: The same object can look different from the top, the front and the side.
The top view is what you see from straight above, like a bird.
The front view is what you see when you stand in front of it.
From one side you see only that side. Things on the other side stay hidden.
A ball looks like a circle from every direction. A dice looks like a square from every direction.

ex.q: Riya stacks 3 cubes one on top of the other to make a tower. What does she see from the top and from the front?
st: From straight above, only the top cube's face shows: 1 square.
From the front, all 3 cubes show, one above the other: 3 squares in a column.
ex.a: Top: 1 square. Front: 3 squares in a column.

topics.rl: Maps and drone photos show places from the top. A photo of your house from the road shows its front view.

rv.summary: The same object can look different from the top, the front and the side. The top view is from straight above; the front view is from standing in front of it.
focus: Give the top, front and side views of everyday objects
Count what can be seen from one view of a tower or a car
Pick an object from two of its views
remember: Top view: what you see from straight above, like a bird
A ball looks like a circle and a dice like a square from every direction
Tower of 3 cubes: top 1 square, front 3 squares in a column
traps: Don't give the top view when the front view is asked
Don't think you can see things on the far side of an object from one side
Check both views, not just one

topics.t: Views of a brick and drawing views
topics.h: Three friends look at the same brick and draw three different rectangles. Who is right? All of them!
p: A brick is a cuboid. From the top, the front and the side, you see three different rectangles.
The one looking from straight above sees the top view. The one in front sees the front view. The one at the end sees the side view.
To draw a view, imagine looking straight at the object from that side and draw only the outline you see.
A pencil lying down looks like a long thin rectangle from the top, but like a small hexagon or circle from its end.

ex.q: A brick lies flat on the ground. Anu looks from the top, Babu from the long front side, Chotu from the short end. Who sees the smallest rectangle?
st: The top is long and wide: biggest rectangle.
The front is long but thin.
The end is short and thin: smallest.
So Chotu sees the smallest rectangle.

topics.rl: Architects draw a top view (plan), a front view and a side view of a house before builders begin work.

rv.summary: A brick is a cuboid, so its top, front and side views are three different rectangles. To draw a view, imagine looking straight at the object from that side and draw only the outline you see.
focus: Match each child to the view they see of a brick
Draw top, front and side views of objects
Know the end view of a lying pencil
remember: Brick: three different rectangles from the top, front and side
Draw only the outline you see from that side
A pencil lying down: long thin rectangle from the top, small hexagon or circle from its end
traps: All views of a brick are not the same
Don't mix up the side view and the top view
Don't draw the front view when the top view is asked

topics.t: Spatial thinking: blocks, places and directions
topics.h: Can you count blocks you cannot even see? Let's play hide and seek with cubes!
p: In a stack, some blocks hide behind or under others. Count row by row and layer by layer.
A wall that is 4 cubes long and 2 cubes high has 4 + 4 = 8 cubes.
Left and right change when you turn around. Things that were on your right are now on your left.
On most maps North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left.
Position words like in front, behind, above, below, left and right help us find things.

ex.q: Arjun builds steps: 3 cubes in the bottom row, 2 in the middle row and 1 on top. How many cubes did he use?

topics.rl: Shopkeepers stack boxes in layers. Auto drivers use left, right and map directions to find your house.

rv.summary: In a stack, some blocks hide behind or under others, so count row by row and layer by layer. Left and right swap when you turn around, and on most maps North is at the top.
focus: Count cubes in walls, steps and blocks, including hidden ones
Work out left and right after turning around
Use map directions: North, South, East, West
remember: Wall 4 cubes long and 2 high: 4 + 4 = 8 cubes
When you turn around, left and right swap
On most maps: North top, South bottom, East right, West left
traps: Don't add length and height; count every row
Don't count only the cubes you can see
Don't mix up East and West

topics.h: The cat is looking for Jagat in class. 'Third desk, second row!' says the teacher. Can you find him?
p: When desks are arranged in rows and columns, they form a grid.
We can say where something is by giving its row number and its desk (column) number.
Always agree where counting starts: for example, row 1 at the front and desk 1 on the left.
To find a spot, first go to the row, then count the desks along it.
Two different positions never point to the same desk; each place has its own row and desk number.

ex.q: In a class grid, row 1 is at the front and desks are counted from the left. Jagat sits in row 2, desk 3. How do you find him?
st: Jagat is at the third desk of the second row.

topics.rl: Cinema seats are marked like 'Row F, seat 12'. Your ticket tells you the row and the seat, just like a grid!

rv.summary: Desks in rows and columns form a grid. We say where something is by its row number and its desk (column) number, after agreeing where counting starts.
focus: Find a thing from its row and column
Give the row and column of a thing
Count all the places in a grid
remember: First go to the row, then count the desks along it
Agree where counting starts, e.g. row 1 at the front, desk 1 on the left
5 rows of 6 desks: 5 × 6 = 30
traps: Don't swap the row and column numbers
Don't count columns from the right when they start from the left
Don't start from the bottom row when row 1 is at the top

topics.t: Grid game: placing things with clues
topics.h: Clue 1: the parrot is in the top-right corner. Clue 2: the mango is just below it. Can you place them all?
p: Corner words help on a grid: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
'Second row, second column' tells the exact box to use.
Some clues compare: 'just below', 'just to the left of', 'in the same row as'.
To solve a puzzle, place the sure things first, then use them to place the rest.

ex.q: On a 3 by 3 grid, the 🦜 is in the top-right corner. The 🥭 is just below the 🦜. Where is the 🥭?
st: Just below means one row down, same column.

topics.rl: Seating plans for a class photo or a school function often use clues like 'tallest in the back row, in the middle'.

topics.h: Your birthday is coming! How many days to wait? The calendar knows!
p: A week has 7 days. A year has 12 months.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days (29 in a leap year). All the other months have 31 days.
A year has 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
The same day of the week comes again every 7 days. If 1 June is a Monday, so are 8, 15, 22 and 29 June.
To count days to a date in the next month, count to the end of this month, then add the days of the next month.

ex.q: Today is 28 March. Aisha's birthday is on 5 April. How many days does she have to wait?

topics.h: If today is Wednesday, what was the day before yesterday? And what will be the day after tomorrow?
p: Yesterday is 1 day before today. The day before yesterday is 2 days before.
Tomorrow is 1 day after today. The day after tomorrow is 2 days after.
The same date moves to a later weekday in the next month. A 31-day month moves it 3 days on; a 30-day month 2 days; a 28-day February 0 days.
Example: 1 January is a Monday. January has 31 days, so 1 February is 3 days later in the week: Thursday.

Yesterday: Tuesday. Day before yesterday: Monday.

topics.h: Baisakhi, Chaitra, Muharram, Ramzan... Different communities in India use their own calendars too!
p: Besides the English calendar, communities use other calendars, like Hindu, Islamic and Sikh calendars, with their own month names and New Year.
Hindu month Chaitra usually falls around March–April. Baisakh (Vaisakh) falls around April–May; Baisakhi is in mid-April.
The Islamic calendar follows the moon. Its months, like Muharram and Ramzan, come about 10 to 11 days earlier every year in the English calendar.
Amavasya (new moon) and Purnima (full moon) repeat in a pattern: each comes about once every 29 to 30 days, about 15 days apart.
Many festivals are fixed by the moon: Diwali is on an Amavasya; Holi and Guru Nanak Jayanti are on a Purnima.

ex.q: Purnima was on 5 March. About when will the next Purnima be?

5 March + about 29 or 30 days → about 3 or 4 April.

p: A day has 24 hours.
From 6 am to 6 pm is 12 hours. From 6 am to the next morning's 6 am is 24 hours.
Add up the hours spent on each activity to see how a day is used.

topics.rl: Grocery shops, restaurants and railway ticket counters all give bills.

rv.summary: A bill lists each item's quantity, rate (price of one) and amount, where amount = quantity × rate. Add all amounts for the total and always check the bill.
focus: Find amounts and totals on a bill
Check a bill for mistakes
Find the change
remember: Amount = quantity × rate
Rate is the price of one item
Change = money given − total
traps: Don't add quantity and rate; multiply
Don't forget to add every item
Don't trust a bill without checking

topics.h: Saving for a model train? Sharing a taxi fare? Money maths helps every day!
p: Add to find a total cost. Subtract to find what is left or how much more is needed.
Multiply when the same price repeats. Divide to share money equally.
When adding rupees and paise, 100 paise make ₹1: ₹10.50 + ₹4.50 = ₹15.00.
To compare deals, find the price of one item in each.

ex.q: Joseph has ₹200. A toy bus costs ₹135. How much money will he have left?

topics.rl: Families share expenses for a trip, save money every week and compare prices before buying.

rv.summary: Add to find a total cost and subtract to find what is left or how much more is needed. Multiply when the same price repeats, divide to share, and compare deals by the price of one item.
focus: Solve money problems with all four operations
Add rupees and paise
Compare deals by the price of one
remember: To compare deals, find the price of one item in each
3 pens for ₹30: each pen costs ₹10
traps: A smaller price is not always cheaper per item
Don't forget that 100 paise make ₹1
Don't give the cost when the change is asked

topics.t: Asking the right question and recording answers
topics.h: 'Do you like school?' or 'Which subject do you like most: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?' Which question gives better data?
p: A good survey question is clear and gives the information you need.
Giving choices helps: 'Which is your favourite subject: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?'
Record answers quickly with short codes: M for Maths, E for English, V for EVS, H for Hindi.
Data can be shown as a long list of codes or as a table of counts. A table is much easier to read.
Choose the way of showing data that answers questions fastest.

ex.q: Codes recorded: M E M V H M E M V M. How many chose Maths?

topics.rl: Teachers, shopkeepers and the government run surveys to plan things like school timetables, stock and new roads.

rv.summary: A good survey question is clear, gives choices and gets the information you need. Record answers quickly with short codes, then show them in a table, which is easier to read than a list.
focus: Choose a clear survey question with choices
Count codes in a list
Know why a table of counts is easier to read
remember: Short codes: M for Maths, E for English, V for EVS, H for Hindi
A table of counts is much easier to read than a long list of codes
traps: A vague or yes/no question cannot show favourites
Don't count all the codes when one subject is asked
Don't pick only the first code as the favourite

topics.h: Which fruit does your class love most? Don't guess. Ask everyone and count. That's data!
p: Data is information we collect, like answers to a question or things we count.
We can collect data by asking people (a survey) or by watching and counting.
Tally marks help us count fast: 4 lines and a 5th line across make a bundle of 5.
We put the counts in a table so it is easy to read and compare.
From a table we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

ex.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part, and which fruit is the favourite?
st: The biggest count is 12, for mango.

topics.rl: Teachers collect data on attendance. Cricket scorers keep data on runs and wickets.

rv.summary: Data is information we collect by asking people (a survey) or by watching and counting. Tally marks help us count fast, and a table makes counts easy to read and compare.
focus: Read tally marks
Find the most, least, total and difference from a table
Choose a good way to collect data
remember: Tally: 4 lines and a 5th line across make a bundle of 5
2 bundles of five and 3 more lines = 13
traps: Don't count each tally bundle as 1
Don't add when the difference is asked
Don't leave out one group in the total

topics.h: Tall bars, short bars! A bar graph lets you compare data in one quick look.
p: A bar graph uses bars to show data. A taller (or longer) bar means a bigger number.
Read the number at the end of each bar using the scale on the side.
The scale can go up in 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s. Check it before reading!
We can use a bar graph to find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

ex.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Monday 4, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 3, Thursday 6. Which day sold the most, and how many were sold in all?

topics.rl: TV news shows bar graphs of rainfall, cricket runs per over and votes.

rv.summary: A bar graph uses bars to show data, and a taller bar means a bigger number. Read the number at the end of each bar using the scale, which can go up in 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s.
focus: Read bar values using the scale
Find the most, least, total and difference
Spot bars of the same height
remember: A taller (or longer) bar means a bigger number
Check the scale before reading
6 lines with each line = 2 students: 12 students
traps: Don't read the line number without using the scale
Don't pick the shortest bar when the most is asked
Don't miss one of the bars in a total

topics.t: Colourful golas: reading and making pictographs
topics.h: The gola-wala sold rose, mango, khus and orange golas. Which flavour should he buy more syrup for?
p: To make a picture chart, colour or draw one symbol for each group of data, using the key.
Read a pictograph: count symbols and multiply by the key value.
The row with the most symbols shows the most popular item; the fewest shows the least.
Use data to decide: buy more of the most popular flavour.
Data can be split into groups, like boys and girls, to compare them separately.

ex.q: Using the gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2), how many mango golas were sold?

topics.rl: Shopkeepers look at what sells most before ordering new stock. That is using data to decide!

rv.summary: Read a pictograph by counting symbols and multiplying by the key value. Use the data to decide things, like buying more of the most popular flavour, and compare groups like boys and girls.
focus: Read pictograph rows using the key
Use data to make a decision
Compare data split into groups
remember: Number = symbols × key value
Most symbols: most popular. Fewest: least popular
Key 🍧 = 2: 4 symbols = 8 golas
traps: Don't count symbols without using the key
Don't use only one group when the total is asked
Don't use the boys' numbers for a question about girls

topics.h: Can a picture of one star stand for 5 children? In a pictograph it can!
p: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how much one symbol stands for, like ⭐ = 5 children.
To read a row, multiply the number of symbols by the key value.
Half a symbol stands for half the key value. If ⭐ = 4, half a star = 2.
To draw a row, divide the number by the key value to find how many symbols.

ex.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?

topics.rl: Newspapers and school notice boards use pictographs to show data in a fun way.

rv.summary: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols, and the key tells how much one symbol stands for. To read a row, multiply the symbols by the key value; to draw a row, divide by it.
focus: Read rows using the key
Read half symbols
Find how many symbols to draw
remember: Read: number of symbols × key value
Half a symbol = half the key value: if ⭐ = 4, half a star = 2
Draw: number ÷ key value
traps: Don't forget the key; each symbol may not mean 1
Don't ignore a half symbol
Give the difference in items, not in symbols

topics.t: Chess or cricket? A survey with two choices
topics.h: Some children play only chess, some only cricket, some both and some neither. How do we sort them?
p: Ask each child two questions: Do you play chess? Do you play cricket?
Sort answers into 4 groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither.
Record the counts in a table.
Children who play chess = only chess + both. Children who play cricket = only cricket + both.

ex.q: Only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3. How many play cricket?

topics.rl: Schools use surveys like this to plan clubs and sports periods.

rv.summary: In a two-choice survey, sort answers into 4 groups: only chess, only cricket, both and neither. Children who play chess = only chess + both.
focus: Sort answers into the 4 groups
Find how many play each game
Find the total asked and how many play only one
remember: Groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither
Chess players = only chess + both. Cricket players = only cricket + both
traps: Don't forget the 'both' group when counting players of a game
Don't leave out the 'neither' group in the total
A child who plays both goes in one group, 'both', not two groups

topics.t: Bal Mela: reading sales over days
topics.h: At the school Bal Mela, popcorn and balloons sold out fast. Which day was the busiest?
p: A pictograph can show sales on different days. Read each day's row using the key.
Total for an item = add all its days. Total for a day = add all items on that day.
The day with the most sales has the biggest total.
Always check the key first: 🍿 = 10 packets means 3 symbols = 30 packets.

ex.q: Using the popcorn pictograph (🍿 = 10), how many packets were sold over the three days?

topics.rl: Organisers of fairs and melas count sales each day to plan stock and stalls for the next year.

rv.summary: A pictograph can show sales on different days; read each row using the key. Total for an item adds all its days, and total for a day adds all items on that day.
focus: Read each day's sales with the key
Find totals for an item and for a day
Find the day with the most sales
remember: Check the key first: 🍿 = 10 means 3 symbols = 30 packets
Item total = add all its days. Day total = add all items that day
traps: Don't count symbols only
Don't add symbols with different keys
Look at all items, not just one, for a day's total

topics.t: Bal Mela: comparing items and completing tables
topics.h: On Wednesday, 40 popcorn packets and 30 balloons were sold. Which sold more, and by how much?
p: To compare two items on the same day, subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
To complete a table from a pictograph, read each row with the key and write the number.
Check the table: the totals in the table must match the pictograph.
A completed table makes it easy to answer questions quickly.

ex.q: On Tuesday, popcorn 50 packets and balloons 15. How many more popcorn packets?

topics.rl: After a mela, teachers make a table of all sales to report to the principal.

rv.summary: To compare two items on the same day, subtract the smaller number from the bigger. To complete a table from a pictograph, read each row with the key, and check the totals match.
focus: Compare two items by subtracting
Fill a table from a pictograph
Find how many symbols to draw from a table
remember: Compare: bigger − smaller
Symbols to draw = number ÷ key value: 40 ÷ 5 = 8
Table totals must match the pictograph
traps: Don't add when comparing
Don't write the number of symbols in the table
Don't draw one symbol per item when the key is 5

qa.q: Qutub Minar is a tall tower that gets thinner as it goes up. Which solid shape do its round sections look like?
qa.e: Each round section of the tower is like a cylinder, and they are stacked one on another.

qa.q: Aman wants a pointed top for his model temple, with a square base. Which block should he use?
qa.e: A square pyramid has a square base and sides that meet at one point, just like a pointed temple top.

qa.q: Which part of a street model could you make with an empty matchbox?
qa.e: A matchbox is a cuboid, like a small shop building.

qa.q: How is a clay model of India Gate DIFFERENT from the real India Gate?
qa.e: A good model copies the shape, but it is much smaller and made of different material.

qa.q: Riya builds a model tower with 3 cylinder blocks stacked on top of each other and 1 cone on the very top. How many blocks does she use?
qa.e: 3 cylinders and 1 cone make 4 blocks.

qa.q: A round dome sits on top of a building. Which solid shape is a dome most like?
qa.e: A dome is round and curved all over, like half a ball (half a sphere).

qa.q: Kabir makes a street model from waste. Which waste item is best for the wheels of a toy bus?
qa.e: Bottle caps are round and flat, just like wheels.

qa.q: For a model gate, Meena uses 2 pillars and 1 cuboid across the top. She makes 3 such gates. How many blocks does she need?
qa.e: Each gate needs 2 + 1 = 3 blocks. 3 gates need 3 × 3 = 9 blocks.

qa.q: How many squares are there in the net of a cube?
qa.e: A cube has 6 square faces, so its net has 6 squares.

qa.q: A net has 2 circles and 1 rectangle. What does it fold into?
qa.e: The rectangle rolls into the curved side and the 2 circles close the top and bottom. That is a cylinder.

qa.q: Aisha looks at a glass standing upright from straight above. What shape does she see?
qa.e: From the top she sees the round rim of the glass, which is a circle.

qa.q: A party cap shaped like a cone stands on its base. What is its front view?
qa.e: From the front, the cap goes from a wide bottom to a point at the top. It looks like a triangle.

qa.q: Kabir looks at a laddoo from the top, the front and the side. What shape does he see every time?
qa.e: A laddoo is a sphere. A sphere looks like a circle from every direction.

qa.q: A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. What does it fold into?
qa.e: The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point. That is a square pyramid.

qa.q: Meena cuts open a cereal box shaped like a cuboid and lays it flat. How many rectangles are in the net?
qa.e: A cuboid has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back and 2 sides. So the net has 6 rectangles.

qa.q: Harpreet looks at a dice lying on a table from straight above. What shape does she see?
qa.e: The top face of a dice is a square, so the top view is a square.

qa.q: How many triangle side faces does a square pyramid have?
qa.e: A square base has 4 sides. Each side has one triangle on it, so there are 4 triangles.

qa.q: What shape are the side faces of a prism?
qa.e: In a prism, the two bases are joined by rectangle side faces.

qa.q: Which solid has all its faces as equal squares?
qa.e: A cube is a special prism with 6 equal square faces.

qa.q: A pyramid has a hexagon as its base. How many triangle faces does it have?
qa.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 triangles, one on each side.

qa.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have in all?
qa.e: It has 2 triangle bases and 3 rectangle sides: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.

qa.q: Ravi folds a net made of 1 triangle in the middle and 3 triangles around it. What does he make?
qa.e: A triangle base with 3 triangles that meet at the top makes a triangular pyramid.

qa.q: The point where all the triangle faces of a pyramid meet is called the...
qa.e: The top point of a pyramid where the triangles meet is the apex.

qa.q: A prism has two pentagon bases. How many rectangle faces join them?
qa.e: Each side of the pentagon is joined by one rectangle, so there are 5 rectangles.

qa.q: How many faces does a dice shaped like a cube have?
qa.e: A cube has 6 faces. That is why a dice has the numbers 1 to 6.

qa.q: How many edges does a cube have?
qa.e: A cube has 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

qa.q: How many corners does a matchbox shaped like a cuboid have?
qa.e: A cuboid has 4 corners on top and 4 on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.

qa.q: Which shape can roll in every direction and has no flat face?
qa.e: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face, so it rolls any way.

qa.q: A tin of oil is shaped like which 3D shape?
qa.e: A tin has a circle at the top, a circle at the bottom and a curved side. That is a cylinder.

qa.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
qa.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces, one at the top and one at the bottom. Its side is curved, not flat.

qa.q: Which 3D shape has one flat circle face and one pointed tip?
qa.e: A cone, like a party cap, has a circle at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top.

qa.q: Joseph has 2 dice. How many faces do the 2 dice have altogether?
qa.e: Each dice has 6 faces. 6 + 6 = 12.

qa.q: In a straw-and-clay model, what does each straw stand for?
qa.e: The straws make the lines of the skeleton, which are the edges.

qa.q: How many clay balls are needed to make the skeleton of a cube?
qa.e: A cube has 8 corners, so it needs 8 clay balls.

qa.q: How many straws are needed for the skeleton of a square pyramid?
qa.e: 4 straws make the square base and 4 more go up to the apex: 4 + 4 = 8.

qa.q: A triangular prism has 5 faces and 6 corners. Use faces + corners − edges = 2 to find its number of edges.
qa.e: 5 + 6 = 11, and 11 − edges = 2, so edges = 9.

qa.q: A solid has 6 faces and 12 edges. How many corners does it have?
qa.e: faces + corners − edges = 2, so 6 + corners − 12 = 2. Corners = 8.

qa.q: Can a solid with only flat faces have exactly 3 faces?
qa.a: No, it needs at least 4 faces
qa.e: Three flat faces cannot close up a solid. The smallest such solid, a triangular pyramid, has 4 faces.

qa.q: Dev has 12 straws and 8 clay balls. He uses all of them. Which skeleton does he make?
qa.e: A cube has 12 edges and 8 corners, matching 12 straws and 8 balls.

qa.q: Pooja joins 4 long paper strips so they cross at the top and bottom, then spreads them out. What shape does she get?
qa.e: Strips crossing at top and bottom and bending outwards look like a ball, a sphere.

qa.q: A dice shows 4 on top. What number is on the bottom face?
qa.e: Opposite faces add up to 7, and 7 − 4 = 3.

qa.q: Which number is opposite 1 on a dice?
qa.e: 1 + 6 = 7, so 6 is opposite 1.

qa.q: Rohan sees 1, 2 and 3 together on one view of a dice. What is the total of the three faces he cannot see?
qa.e: The hidden faces are 6, 5 and 4 (opposites of 1, 2, 3). 6 + 5 + 4 = 15.

qa.q: Which face of a dice does NOT share an edge with the face showing 3?
qa.e: Only the opposite face does not touch it. 3 + 4 = 7, so 4 is opposite 3.

qa.q: Which of these is a neighbour (shares an edge) of the face with 6?
qa.e: 6 is opposite 1, so every other face, including 2, touches 6.

qa.q: The top and bottom faces of a dice together always make what total?
qa.e: Top and bottom are opposite, and opposite faces always add to 7.

qa.q: A cube has 6 colours. In 3 views, red is seen with blue, green, yellow and white. Which colour is opposite red if the 6th colour is black?
qa.e: Colours seen with red are its neighbours. The only colour never seen with red is black, so black is opposite.

qa.q: Two dice lie on a table. What is the total of the two bottom faces if the top faces show 5 and 6?
qa.e: Bottom of 5 is 2, bottom of 6 is 1. 2 + 1 = 3.

qa.q: Which solid has only a curved surface and no flat face?
qa.e: A sphere is curved all over. Cylinders and cones also have flat faces.

qa.q: Which solid has BOTH flat faces and a curved surface?
qa.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved surface.

qa.q: In a Venn diagram, one circle is 'has square faces' and the other is 'has triangle faces'. Where does a triangular pyramid go?
qa.e: All 4 faces of a triangular pyramid are triangles. It has no square face, so it goes only in 'has triangle faces'.

qa.q: Same circles: 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'. Where does a cylinder go?
qa.e: A cylinder has circle faces and a curved surface, so it fits neither rule and goes outside both circles.

qa.q: Which shape goes in the overlap of 'has square faces' and 'has triangle faces'?
qa.e: A square pyramid has a square base and triangle sides, so it fits both circles.

qa.q: I have 6 faces. All of them are rectangles, and they are not all squares. What am I?
qa.e: 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares make a cuboid, like a brick.

qa.q: A solid has 4 faces, all triangles. What is it?
qa.e: A triangular pyramid has a triangle base and 3 triangle sides: 4 triangles in all.

qa.q: How many of these have only flat faces: cube, cone, cuboid, sphere, square pyramid?
qa.e: Cube, cuboid and square pyramid have only flat faces. That is 3.

qa.q: A block is 2 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 2 cubes high. How many cubes are in it?
qa.e: Each layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes. 2 layers make 8 cubes. One is hidden at the back.

qa.q: In that 2 × 2 × 2 block, you can see 7 cubes. How many cubes are hidden?
qa.e: 8 cubes in all, 7 can be seen, so 8 − 7 = 1 is hidden.

qa.q: A staircase has 4 cubes at the bottom, 3 in the next row, 2 next and 1 on top, all in one line from the front. How many cubes?
When one cube is drawn on triangular dot paper, how many of its faces show in the drawing?
qa.e: The drawing shows the top and two sides, so 3 faces.

qa.q: Which of these flat shapes will NOT fold into a cube?
qa.e: A straight line of 6 squares overlaps itself when folded and cannot close.

qa.q: Priya's cube net has only 5 squares. What will happen when she folds it?
qa.e: A cube needs 6 faces. With 5 squares, one face is missing, like an open box.

qa.q: A square pyramid net is missing one triangle. How many triangles does it have now?
qa.e: A square pyramid net has 1 square and 4 triangles. One missing leaves 4 − 1 = 3.

qa.q: A tower is 3 cubes high. Next to it is a tower 2 cubes high. Behind both, hidden, is a tower of 4 cubes. How many cubes altogether?
qa.e: 3 + 2 + 4 = 9, including the hidden tower.

qa.q: What is made where two straight lines meet at a point?
qa.e: When two lines meet at a point they make an angle.

qa.q: How many angles does a triangle have?
qa.e: A triangle has 3 corners, and each corner is an angle.

qa.q: How do you make a right angle checker from a piece of paper?
qa.a: Fold it twice, the second fold along the first folded edge
qa.e: Fold once to get a straight edge, then fold that edge onto itself. The corner is a right angle.

qa.q: Which of these makes a right angle?
qa.e: At 3:00 the hands make a square corner, a right angle.

qa.q: Zoya puts her right angle checker on the corner of her school bag tag. It fits exactly. What does this tell her?
qa.a: The corner is a right angle
qa.e: If the checker fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.

qa.q: A drawing shows 2 triangles and 1 square. How many angles are there in all?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 angles and the square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10.

qa.q: On a dot grid, Rahul draws a line straight across and another straight up from the same dot. What angle does he make?
qa.e: Across and straight up make a square corner, a right angle.

qa.q: How many right angles does a rectangle-shaped blackboard have?
qa.e: A rectangle has 4 corners, and all 4 are right angles.

qa.q: An angle is smaller than a right angle. What type of angle is it?
qa.e: Angles smaller than a right angle are acute.

qa.q: An angle is bigger than a right angle but less than a straight line. What is it called?
qa.e: Bigger than a right angle means obtuse.

qa.q: What type of angle do the clock hands make at 4:00?
qa.e: At 3:00 it is a right angle. At 4:00 the hands are wider apart, so the angle is obtuse.

qa.q: The angle at the bottom tip of the letter V is...
qa.e: The two lines of V meet in a sharp point, smaller than a right angle.

qa.q: Which capital letter has a right angle?
qa.e: The two lines of L meet in a square corner.

qa.q: Rani draws a line. She wants to draw an obtuse angle from one end. How should the second line go?
qa.a: Opening wide, more than a square corner
qa.e: An obtuse angle opens wider than a right angle.

qa.q: A shape has 3 angles. One is a right angle and the other two are acute. What shape is it?
qa.e: Any shape with 3 angles is a triangle. This one is a right triangle.

qa.q: A shape has 4 equal sides. Two angles are acute and two are obtuse. Which shape is it?
qa.e: 4 equal sides like a square, but pushed so the angles are not right angles: a rhombus.

qa.q: Meera colours acute angles red, right angles blue and obtuse angles green. Her rhombus has 2 acute and 2 obtuse angles. How many angles are green?
qa.e: Obtuse angles are coloured green. The rhombus has 2 obtuse angles, so 2 are green (and 2 are red).

qa.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
qa.e: A hexagon has 6 straight sides and 6 corners.

qa.q: A rangoli tile has 5 straight sides. What is the name of this shape?
qa.e: A flat shape with 5 straight sides is a pentagon.

qa.q: How many corners does a circle have?
qa.e: A circle has one curved edge and no corners at all.

qa.q: Riya joins 3 straight sticks end to end to make a closed shape. Which shape does she get?
qa.e: 3 straight sides joined in a closed shape make a triangle.

qa.q: Arjun draws 2 triangles and 1 square. How many sides is that altogether?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 sides and the square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10.

qa.q: Which of these is a flat 2D shape?
qa.e: A square drawn on paper is flat. A ball, a dice and a tin are solid 3D objects.

qa.q: Kabir draws a square with each side 5 cm long. What is the total length of all its sides?
qa.e: A square has 4 equal sides. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 cm.

qa.q: Meena counts all the corners of one square and one triangle. How many corners does she count?
qa.e: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3 corners. 4 + 3 = 7.

qa.q: Which straw shape stays firm and does not change shape when pushed?
qa.e: A triangle is rigid: its three sides lock its angles.

qa.q: When a straw square is pushed at one corner, what changes?
qa.e: The straws stay the same length, but the angles change.

qa.q: What is true about all the angles of a rectangle?
qa.e: A rectangle has 4 right angles.

qa.q: Why are electric towers built with many triangles?
qa.a: Triangles keep their shape and make the tower strong
qa.e: Triangles are rigid, so the tower does not bend out of shape.

qa.q: On a dot grid, Kavya draws a 4-sided shape with all right angles. Two sides are 3 dots apart and two are 5 dots apart. What is it?
qa.e: 4 right angles with opposite sides equal but not all sides equal: a rectangle.

qa.q: How many angles does a 5-sided shape have?
qa.e: A shape has as many angles as sides, so 5 angles.

qa.q: Which shape has MORE than 5 angles?
qa.e: A hexagon has 6 angles. The others have 3 or 4.

qa.q: Arun draws a triangle, a square and a hexagon. How many of them have fewer than 5 angles?
qa.e: The triangle (3) and the square (4) have fewer than 5 angles. The hexagon has 6.

qa.q: Hari makes a pentagon with 5 equal straws and pushes one corner. What happens?
qa.a: The angles change but the sides stay the same length
qa.e: Like a square, a straw pentagon is not rigid. The straws keep their length, but the angles change when it is pushed.

qa.q: A circle has a radius of 6 cm. What is its diameter?
qa.e: The diameter is twice the radius: 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

qa.q: A round roti is 20 cm across through the centre. What is its radius?
qa.e: 20 cm across is the diameter. Radius = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm.

qa.q: Sunita folds a paper circle exactly in half. What does the fold line show?
qa.e: A fold that splits a circle into two equal halves passes through the centre. It is a diameter.

qa.q: Two different diameters are drawn on one circle. Where do they cross?
qa.e: Every diameter passes through the centre, so all diameters meet there.

qa.q: Kiran puts 8 straws, each 10 cm long, around a point like the spokes of a wheel. Their outer ends lie on a circle. Why?
qa.a: Every end is the same distance, 10 cm, from the centre
qa.e: All points of a circle are the same distance from the centre. Equal straws put every end at 10 cm.

qa.q: Wheel A has a radius of 35 cm. Wheel B has a diameter of 60 cm. Which wheel is bigger?
qa.e: Wheel A's diameter is 2 × 35 = 70 cm, which is more than 60 cm. So A is bigger.

qa.q: A round carpet has a design line from its centre to its edge that is 75 cm long. What is the carpet's diameter?
qa.e: Centre to edge is the radius. Diameter = 2 × 75 = 150 cm.

qa.q: How many diameters can be drawn in a circle?
qa.e: You can draw a diameter through the centre in any direction, so there are very many, all equal.

qa.q: Asha has no compass. She wants to draw a circle of radius 5 cm. She marks a centre dot. What should she do next?
qa.a: Mark many points 5 cm from the dot and join them smoothly
qa.e: Every point of a circle is the same distance from the centre. Many points 5 cm from the dot, joined smoothly, make the circle.

qa.q: A square has one diagonal drawn. How many triangles do you see?
qa.e: The diagonal joins opposite corners and cuts the square into 2 triangles.

qa.q: A square has BOTH diagonals drawn. How many triangles are there in all?
qa.e: 4 small triangles, plus 4 bigger triangles each made of 2 small ones: 4 + 4 = 8.

qa.q: A triangle has 2 lines drawn from its top corner to its base. How many triangles are there in all?
qa.e: 3 small triangles, 2 made of 2 small ones next to each other, and 1 big one: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

qa.q: Leela has 5 matchsticks. How many triangles can she make side by side, sharing sticks?
qa.e: The first triangle needs 3 sticks. The second shares a side and needs only 2 more: 3 + 2 = 5.

qa.q: A row of 3 triangles side by side is made with 7 matchsticks. If you remove one outer stick of the last triangle (a stick it does not share), how many triangles are left?
qa.e: Removing a side of the end triangle breaks it, leaving 2 triangles.

qa.q: Ankit cuts a square on a dot grid along one diagonal. What two shapes does he get?
qa.e: A diagonal cut joins opposite corners and makes 2 triangles.

qa.q: A big right-angled triangle has a square cut out at its right-angled corner. The far corner of the square just touches the slanting side. What shapes are left over?
qa.e: When a square is cut from the corner of a triangle, the leftover pieces are smaller triangles.

qa.q: Diya wants to trace a square with one diagonal without lifting her pencil or going over a line twice. Where should she start?
qa.a: At a corner where 3 lines meet
qa.e: The two ends of the diagonal have 3 lines each. Start at one of them and finish at the other.

qa.q: A drawing of a house has a square wall, a triangle roof, a rectangle door and a round window. How many different kinds of shapes are hidden in it?
qa.e: Square, triangle, rectangle and circle: 4 different kinds of shapes.

qa.q: A ball is under a chair. Which sentence is correct?
qa.a: The ball is below the seat of the chair
qa.e: Under the chair means the ball is below the seat.

qa.q: Sonu stands in front of a big truck. Tina is hiding behind the truck. Can Sonu see Tina?
qa.e: The truck is between them, so it hides Tina from Sonu.

qa.q: Where can the seeker go to see children hiding behind the bushes in a park?
qa.a: Up on a high slide looking down
qa.e: From high above, you can see over the bushes.

qa.q: Gita is between Ali and Bina in a line. Who is in the middle?
qa.e: Between two people means in the middle of them.

qa.q: A cat sits on top of a cupboard. A dog sleeps on the floor in front of the cupboard. Which is true?
qa.a: The cat is above the dog
qa.e: The cat is on top of the cupboard, high up, so it is above the dog.

qa.q: Mohit hides behind a pillar. The seeker walks round to the other side of the pillar. What happens?
qa.a: The seeker can now see Mohit
qa.e: From the other side, the pillar is no longer between them.

qa.q: From a drone high above a playground, which of these can be seen?
qa.a: Children behind a wall, and the tops of everything
qa.e: From directly above, walls do not hide the ground behind them.

qa.q: Four children hide: one under a table, one behind a door, one beside a sofa, one in front of a window. Who can the seeker standing at the window easily see?
qa.a: The one in front of the window
qa.e: The child in front of the window is right near the seeker with nothing blocking the view.

qa.q: From straight above, what shape does a bucket standing upright look like?
qa.e: Looking down into a bucket you see its round rim, which is a circle.

qa.q: Arjun stands in front of a tall water tank shaped like a cylinder. What shape does he see?
qa.e: From the front, a standing cylinder has a straight side, a flat top and a flat bottom, so it looks like a rectangle.

qa.q: Aisha looks at a car from one side. How many wheels can she see?
qa.e: A car has 2 wheels on each side. From one side the other 2 wheels are hidden.

qa.q: Kabir stacks 4 cubes one on top of the other. Looking from straight above, how many cube faces can he see?
qa.e: From the top he sees only the top face of the highest cube. The others are hidden below it.

qa.q: Kabir looks at the same tower of 4 cubes from the front. How many squares does he see?
qa.e: From the front, every cube in the tower shows one face. So he sees 4 squares, one above the other.

qa.q: A bird flying over a house sees its roof. What do we call this view?
qa.e: Looking from straight above is called the top view.

qa.q: Which object looks like a circle from the top AND a rectangle from the front?
qa.e: A glass is a cylinder: round from the top, rectangle from the front. A ball is a circle both ways, a dice is a square, and a cap is a triangle from the front.

qa.q: Meena holds a round steel plate flat and looks at it exactly from the side, at eye level. What does she see?
qa.e: A plate is very thin. From the side you see only its thin edge, like a flat strip.

qa.q: A brick lies flat on a table. Which child sees its biggest rectangle?
qa.a: The one looking from the top
qa.e: A flat brick shows its biggest face on top, the long and wide face.

qa.q: What shape is the top view of a water bottle standing on a table?
qa.e: Looking down on a round bottle, you see a circle.

qa.q: A six-sided pencil lies on the table. What do you see from its sharpened end, looking straight at the tip?
qa.a: A small hexagon with a point in the middle
qa.e: From the end, you look at the six-sided pencil, so you see a hexagon with the tip in the middle.

qa.q: A cap with a round top and a front peak is seen from the top. What do you see?
qa.a: A circle with the peak sticking out
qa.e: From above you see the round crown and the peak sticking out in front.

qa.q: Which view of a chair shows its back as a tall shape and its seat as a thin line?
qa.e: From the side, the back stands up tall and the seat looks like a thin line.

qa.q: Three children see a brick and draw: a big rectangle, a long thin rectangle, a small rectangle. How many different views did they draw?
qa.e: Top, front and side views are three different rectangles.

qa.q: Which object looks like a circle from the top and a rectangle from the side?
qa.e: A standing tin can (cylinder) is round from the top and a rectangle from the side.

qa.q: To draw the front view of a cupboard, where should you imagine standing?
qa.e: The front view is what you see when you face the object from the front.

qa.q: A wall of cubes is 5 cubes long and 2 cubes high. How many cubes are in the wall?
qa.e: Each row has 5 cubes and there are 2 rows. 5 + 5 = 10.

qa.q: Steps are built with 4 cubes at the bottom, then 3, then 2, then 1 on top. How many cubes in all?
qa.e: Add every row: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

qa.q: Riya faces the school gate and the library is on her right. She turns around to face the other way. Where is the library now?
qa.e: When you turn around, left and right swap. So the library is now on her left.

qa.q: Joseph builds a block with 2 layers. Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes. How many cubes did he use?
qa.e: One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes. Two layers have 4 + 4 = 8 cubes, even though some are hidden inside.

qa.q: 7 children stand in a row. Meena is 3rd from the left. What is her place counting from the right?
qa.e: There are 2 children to her left, so there are 7 - 3 = 4 children to her right. She comes next, so she is 5th from the right.

qa.q: On a map, North is at the top. Which direction is on the right side of the map?
qa.e: With North at the top, East is on the right, West on the left and South at the bottom.

qa.q: Harpreet looks in a mirror and raises her right hand. If the girl in the mirror were a real girl facing Harpreet, which of her hands would be up?
qa.e: A mirror flips left and right. The girl in the mirror faces Harpreet, so the raised hand is her left hand.

qa.q: Kabir walks 4 steps forward and then 4 steps back. How many steps away from the start is he?
qa.e: Going 4 steps back undoes the 4 steps forward. He is back at the start, 0 steps away.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. What is in row 2, column 2?
qa.e: Go to row 2 (🌸 🐶 📘) and count 2 from the left: 🐶.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Where is the ⭐?
qa.e: ⭐ is in row 3, and it is the second from the left.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. What is in row 1, column 1?
qa.e: Row 1 is the top row and column 1 is the first from the left: 🐱.

qa.q: A class has 5 rows with 6 desks in each row. How many desks are there?
qa.e: 5 rows of 6 desks: 5 × 6 = 30.

qa.q: Row 1 is at the front. Desks are counted from the left. Simran sits in row 4, desk 1. Where is she?
qa.a: Fourth row, first desk on the left
qa.e: Row 4 means the fourth row from the front. Desk 1 is the first on the left.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Which choice correctly describes where the 📘 is?
qa.e: 📘 is in row 2, third from the left.

qa.q: Peter draws a 3 by 3 grid and must put a 🏏 at row 3, column 1 (row 1 at the top). Where should he draw it?
qa.e: Row 3 is the bottom row, and column 1 is on the left: the bottom-left box.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. How many things are in column 3?
qa.e: Column 3 has ⚽, 📘 and 🥭: 3 things, one in each row.

qa.q: On a 3 by 3 grid with row 1 at the top, where is the bottom-right corner?
qa.e: Bottom means row 3 and right means column 3.

qa.q: Place a 🌙 in the second row, second column of a 3 by 3 grid. Which box is that?
qa.e: Row 2, column 2 is right in the middle of a 3 by 3 grid.

qa.q: Clues: 🐘 is in the top-left corner. 🐯 is just to the right of 🐘. Where is 🐯 (row 1 at top)?
qa.e: Top-left is row 1, column 1. One to the right is row 1, column 2.

qa.q: Clues: ⭐ is in the centre of a 3 by 3 grid. 🌸 is just above ⭐. Where is 🌸?
qa.e: Centre is row 2, column 2. Just above is one row up: row 1, column 2.

qa.q: Clues: the 🍌 is in the bottom row. It is in the same column as the top-right corner. Where is the 🍌?
qa.e: Top-right corner is in column 3. Bottom row is row 3. So row 3, column 3.

qa.q: A 4 by 4 grid has 4 rows and 4 columns. How many boxes does it have?
qa.e: 4 rows of 4 boxes: 4 × 4 = 16.

qa.q: Clues on a 3 by 3 grid: 🍎 and 🍇 are in the top row. 🍎 is in a corner on the left. 🍇 is in the middle of the row. Which box of the top row is empty?
qa.e: 🍎 is in column 1 and 🍇 is in column 2, so column 3 is empty.

qa.q: Clues: 🚲 is in row 2. 🚲 is in the column just left of the centre column of a 3 by 3 grid. Where is 🚲?
qa.e: The centre column is column 2. Just left of it is column 1. So row 2, column 1.

qa.q: Start at row 3, column 1 of a 3 by 3 grid (row 1 at top). Move 2 steps right. Where are you?
qa.e: Right keeps the row the same. Column 1 + 2 = column 3.

qa.q: Start at row 3, column 1. Move 2 steps up (row 1 at top). Where are you?
qa.e: Up takes you towards row 1: row 3 → row 2 → row 1. Column stays 1.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Start at 🚗. Move 1 step right, then 1 step up. Where are you?
qa.e: 🚗 → 1 right is ⭐ → 1 up is 🐶.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Start at 🐱. Move 2 steps right, then 2 steps down. Which thing do you reach?
qa.e: 🐱 → 2 right is ⚽ → 2 down is 🥭.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Ravi starts at 🌸 and tells Sita how to reach 📘. Which moves are correct?
qa.e: 🌸 and 📘 are in the same row. 📘 is 2 columns to the right.

qa.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Mini started at 🍎 and moved 1 down, then 1 right. What was her target?
qa.e: 🍎 → 1 down is 🐶 → 1 right is 📘.

qa.q: Ali moves 4 steps right, 3 steps up and 1 step left on a grid. How many steps does he walk in all?
qa.e: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 steps walked.

qa.q: From the start, Neha moves 5 steps right and then 2 steps left. How many columns to the right of the start is she now?
qa.e: 5 right then 2 left leaves her 5 − 2 = 3 columns to the right.

qa.q: A path goes 4 steps right and 3 steps up. How many steps long is it?
qa.e: 4 + 3 = 7 steps.

qa.q: Path A is 5 steps. Path B is 8 steps. Both reach the well. How many steps shorter is path A?
qa.e: 8 − 5 = 3 steps shorter.

qa.q: The park is 2 right and 5 up from home. The shop is 3 right and 3 up. Which is nearer to home?
qa.e: Park: 2 + 5 = 7 steps. Shop: 3 + 3 = 6 steps. 6 is less, so the shop is nearer.

qa.q: Rekha goes 3 right, 2 up. Mohan goes to the same place by 3 up, 1 right, 1 down, 2 right. Who walks more steps?
qa.e: Rekha: 3 + 2 = 5. Mohan: 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 7. Mohan walks more because of his detour.

qa.q: On a grid, the shortest path from the gate to the tap is 4 steps right and 2 steps up. How many steps is the shortest path?
qa.e: A path that never goes back is 4 + 2 = 6 steps.

qa.q: A path goes 2 right, 1 up, 2 right, 1 up. Another goes 4 right, 2 up. Which is longer?
qa.e: First: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6. Second: 4 + 2 = 6. They are equal because neither goes backwards.

qa.q: The swing is 6 steps away. The slide is 9 steps away. How many more steps to the slide than to the swing?
qa.e: 9 − 6 = 3 more steps.

qa.q: Which path is the shortest from start to finish, if finish is 3 right and 3 up?
qa.e: 3 + 3 = 6 steps. The other paths go backwards and are longer.

qa.q: What do we call a view of a place from directly above?
qa.e: Looking from directly above, like a flying bird, gives a bird's-eye (top) view.

qa.q: In a drone photo, a round water tank looks like a...
qa.e: The top of a round tank is a circle.

qa.q: What is a map?
qa.a: A top-view drawing that shows where things are
qa.e: A map is a top-view drawing of a place showing where things are.

qa.q: In an aerial picture of a school, you see a long rectangle roof next to a big open ground with goal posts. The long roof is most likely...
qa.e: A long rectangle roof near the ground is likely a building such as a classroom block.

qa.q: Why is a map useful?
qa.a: It shows where places are, so we can find our way
qa.e: A map shows positions of places, which helps us find routes.

qa.q: From above, what can a drone see that a child on the ground cannot?
qa.e: From high above, a wall does not block the view of what is behind it.

qa.q: On a school map, the library is drawn to the left of the office. In the real school, where is the library?
qa.a: To the left of the office
qa.e: Maps keep things in the same positions as in real life.

qa.q: A cricket ground seen from a helicopter looks like a...
qa.e: From above, the cricket ground is a big oval of grass.

qa.q: Route 1 from home to school is 8 blocks. Route 2 is 11 blocks. Which is shorter and by how much?
qa.e: 8 is less than 11, and 11 − 8 = 3.

qa.q: There are 2 roads from the house to the main road, and 3 roads from the main road to the market. How many different routes are there from the house to the market through the main road?
qa.e: Each of the 2 first roads can join any of the 3 next roads: 2 × 3 = 6 routes.

qa.q: Route A: 4 blocks. Route B: 4 blocks then 2 blocks back then 2 blocks forward. Which is longer?
qa.e: Route B is 4 + 2 + 2 = 8 blocks. Route A is only 4.

qa.q: Why is a straight route usually the shortest?
qa.a: It does not go back or around
qa.e: Going back or around adds extra steps. A straight route avoids that.

qa.q: To get from the canteen to the gate, Rahul's route is 3 + 2 + 4 blocks. Sana's route is 5 + 3 blocks. Who walks less?
qa.e: Rahul: 3 + 2 + 4 = 9. Sana: 5 + 3 = 8. Sana walks less.

qa.q: A map shows 3 routes from the gate to the hall: 6, 5 and 7 steps. How many steps is the shortest route?
qa.e: The smallest of 6, 5 and 7 is 5.

qa.q: On a map, you trace a route from the gate. What should your finger do?
qa.a: Move along the paths from the start to the end
qa.e: Tracing means following the paths step by step from start to end.

qa.q: Route X is 12 steps. Route Y is 3 steps longer than X. How long is route Y?
qa.e: 3 steps longer means 12 + 3 = 15.

qa.q: Which is the clearest direction for a new student?
qa.a: Go straight, turn right at the water cooler, second door on the left
qa.e: It uses clear moves and a landmark.

qa.q: Kiran walks north and turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
qa.e: Facing north, your right hand points east. Turning right makes you face east.

qa.q: What is a landmark?
qa.a: An easy-to-spot place used in directions
qa.e: A landmark is a place that is easy to see, like a statue or a big tree.

qa.q: Meena is walking towards the school gate. The temple is on her left. She turns around and walks back. Where is the temple now?
qa.e: Turning around swaps left and right.

qa.q: Sachin draws a map of his school. What must he do so others can use it?
qa.a: Put places in the right positions and label them
qa.e: A useful map shows places in their correct positions with labels.

qa.q: Directions: 'From the gate, go straight 2 blocks, turn left, go 1 block.' How many blocks do you walk?
qa.e: 2 + 1 = 3 blocks.

qa.q: On your map, the office is in front of the gate and the canteen is to the right of the office. A friend at the gate facing the office wants the canteen. What do you say?
qa.a: Go straight to the office, then turn right
qa.e: First reach the office by going straight, then the canteen is on the right.

qa.q: Abdul's directions say 'turn left' three times in a row on a square path around a park. After the third left turn, compared to the start, which way does he face?
qa.a: Right of where he started facing
qa.e: Each left turn is a quarter turn. Three left quarter turns face the same way as one right turn.

qa.q: A field has 9 rows of trees with 9 trees in each row. How many trees are there?
qa.e: 9 rows of 9 is 9 × 9 = 81.

qa.q: Find 81 × 5 by splitting 81 into 80 and 1.
Plates are kept in 3 stacks of 6, 4 and 5 plates. How many plates in all?
qa.e: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15 plates.

qa.q: A sweet box has 4 rows with 5 laddoos in each row. Amma buys 3 such boxes. How many laddoos?
qa.e: One box: 4 × 5 = 20. Three boxes: 20 × 3 = 60.

qa.q: Which is the quickest way to count 7 rows of 8 chairs?
qa.e: Equal rows can be counted by multiplying: 7 × 8 = 56.
